layers.description: Parent and subtask structure, typed dependencies with lead and lag, and the reference to an independently versioned plan.

findings.name: Parent, subtasks and grouping
findings.description: How a task sits inside a parent, project or work order, how subtasks execute, and how their outcomes assemble into the parent result.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Containment is a typed edge between independently identified task, project and work order records; the parent and the child are each their own artifact. Materialising the hierarchy as a further artifact would create a third copy of a relationship already asserted at both ends, so the edge set is governed with the dependency graph artifact instead.

findings.name: Typed dependencies, lead and lag
findings.description: How ordering constraints between tasks are typed, how lead or lag is expressed, and how cycles and cross-system references are handled.

findings.name: Reference to plan or schedule
findings.description: How the task points at an independently versioned plan, and which side prevails when planned and actual timing disagree.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The plan or schedule is an independently versioned artifact owned by the sibling model WM-ACT-008, consistent with the registered REFERENCE relation. The task holds only a version-pinned reference plus a computed variance value; copying plan content into the task would create a second, silently stale master for the schedule.

bundles.name: Work content, results and evidence
bundles.description: What goes into the task, what counts as done, what comes out, and what proves it happened.
bundles.rationale: FHIR, WS-HumanTask and A2A all model typed inputs and outputs plus completion behaviour, and PROV-O supplies the used and generated relations that connect them. Acceptance, measurement and evidence are separable concerns that determine whether a completion claim can be trusted.

layers.name: Inputs, acceptance criteria and execution constraints
layers.description: What must be supplied, what must be true to call the work done, and the conditions and resources execution requires.

findings.name: Typed inputs, parameters and subject focus
findings.description: The typed information a task consumes, when each value is bound, what the task acts upon, and how inputs are validated.

findings.name: Completion criteria, acceptance and verification
findings.description: What must hold for the task to count as complete, who accepts the result, and whether acceptance is separate from completion.

findings.name: Preconditions, resources, instruments and location
findings.description: The conditions that must hold to execute, the resources and instruments required, and where performance must take place.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Preconditions, resource needs and location are inline structured constraints evaluated against the task record. The resources and places themselves are governed by sibling asset, facility and party models, and reservations are their records, not the task's, so no artifact is minted here.

layers.name: Outputs and measurement
layers.description: What the task produces and how progress and effort are quantified.

findings.name: Outputs, produced artifacts and derivation
findings.description: What the task produces, how each output is identified and linked to the inputs it came from, and whether outputs may change after closure.

findings.name: Progress reporting and effort accounting
findings.description: How progress is quantified, what effort was estimated and consumed, and how far a self-reported figure can be trusted.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Progress and effort are inline scalar measurements on the task record; only percent complete has direct normative support in the sources examined. Detailed time recording, rates and cost belong to a sibling effort and cost model, so no artifact is minted here and the effort fields are declared a supported gap.

layers.name: Provenance and evidence
layers.description: Who did what, using what, and what proves the claim.

findings.name: Execution provenance and attribution
findings.description: Which agent performed each step, in which role and on whose behalf, and which entities were used and generated.

findings.name: Evidence capture, integrity and sufficiency
findings.description: What evidence must be captured to prove the work was done as specified, how its integrity is protected, and who judges sufficiency.

bundles.name: Access, retention and interoperability
bundles.description: Who may see and change the task, how long it is kept, and how it exchanges safely with other systems.
bundles.rationale: NIST establishes access control and audit accountability as required control families; iCalendar and FHIR carry confidentiality classification; A2A, OSLC and iCalendar each define exchange controls such as sequence numbers and terminal-state immutability. Governance and exchange integrity are therefore modelled explicitly rather than left to the storage projection.

layers.name: Access, confidentiality and retention
layers.description: Visibility rules, classification, exceptional access, and how long task content survives closure.

findings.name: Visibility, classification and exceptional access
findings.description: Who may see or change the task and its content, what classification applies, and how emergency access is authorised and reviewed.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Access decisions are enforced at runtime by the interface projection and are recorded on the existing transition and audit log artifact; the authorisation policy itself is a governance document owned by the adopting Dimension's policy model. The task therefore carries only an inline classification code and grant records, with no artifact of its own.

findings.name: Personal data, retention period and erasure
findings.description: Which task fields can carry personal data, how long the record and its history are kept, and how deletion is performed without destroying audit integrity.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Retention is expressed as inline classification codes and dates on the record, plus a tombstone entry on the existing audit log. The retention schedule and the legal basis for holding performer-identifying data are jurisdiction-specific governance instruments of the adopting Dimension; no legislative source was retrieved in this pass, so this model deliberately mints no artifact and asserts no statutory period.

layers.name: Alignment and exchange integrity
layers.description: Crosswalks to external task vocabularies and the controls that keep exchanged copies consistent.

findings.name: Alignment crosswalks and conformance evidence
findings.description: Which external vocabularies the model is aligned to, which fields and states survive a round trip, and what evidence any conformance claim rests on.

findings.name: Concurrency, idempotency and ordering on exchange
findings.description: How competing updates, duplicate requests and out-of-order status delivery are detected and resolved between systems.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Concurrency and idempotency controls are inline scalars on the record and headers of whichever access interface is used; they are meaningless outside the record whose version they identify. Rejected and duplicate updates are captured on the existing transition log rather than in a dedicated artifact.

model.name: Observation / Measurement Record
model.purpose: Provide a format-neutral context structure for a single observation act and the measurement record it produces, binding a feature of interest, an observable property, an observing procedure, a result value and its unit, together with time, uncertainty, quality, provenance and governance context, so that an AI agent can create, inspect, validate and operate observation records without owning the lifecycles of the sensors, samples, methods or catalogues it references.
model.scope_statement: The subject is the observation event and its resulting record: the act of determining a value for an observable property of a feature of interest by applying an observing procedure, plus everything needed to interpret, trust, correlate and retire that single record. OMS/ISO 19156 and SOSA/SSN both model an Observation as an execution (an act), so this model is an event, not the sensor, the sample, the property definition or the dataset. It carries references, bindings and observation-specific parameters for those neighbours; it does not reproduce their identity, lifecycle or operational machinery. Storage and interface (JSON, XML, RDF, Markdown, Git, MCP, MongoDB, relational LIMS tables) are projections of this semantics, never part of it.
in_scope: Identity, versioning and classification of one observation record and of the observation act it documents
Binding to exactly one observable property and one observing procedure, and to the observer, host and deployment that executed it, by reference
Proximate and ultimate feature of interest, and the reference to the sample or sampling chain when observation is indirect
Result representation: value, datatype, cardinality, complex or coverage payloads, and the unit of measure or quantity-kind binding
Absent, censored, below-detection-limit, out-of-range and non-numeric results, with the reason they are absent or bounded
Measurement uncertainty statements (standard, expanded, coverage factor and coverage probability) recorded against the result
References to metrological traceability chains and calibration evidence held by other models
Reference ranges, interpretation codes and recorded statements of conformity together with the identifier of the decision rule applied
Temporal frame: phenomenon time, result time, valid time and ingestion or observation-capture time, each with explicit offsets
Aggregation duration, interpolation type, cumulative flags and sampling regime that determine how the value may be resampled
Observation geometry, observed area and the environmental or operating conditions in force during the act
Record lifecycle status, amendment, correction, supersession and retraction semantics for this record only
Recorded quality flags and quality-control outcomes produced elsewhere, plus references to the evidence supporting them
Provenance chain, derivation from prior observations, responsible agents, ownership and attribution
Access classification, retention binding, and identifier resolution and cross-system correlation
Alignment declarations and encoding bindings to external observation standards, and membership in collections, datastreams or series
out_of_scope: The sensor, instrument or observing system as a managed asset, including its own registration, maintenance, firmware and decommissioning lifecycle
Calibration and traceability records as governed documents: this model references a calibration certificate but does not issue, renew, revoke or verify one
The sample or specimen as an entity, including collection, preparation, custody transfer, storage and disposal lifecycle
Definition and governance of observable properties, quantity kinds and controlled vocabularies, including term proposal, deprecation and mapping maintenance
Unit-of-measure registry maintenance, unit conversion tables and dimensional-analysis services
The observing procedure or test method as a controlled specification, including method development, validation studies and version approval
Execution of quality-control tests, rule evaluation, thresholding or automated flagging: this model records the outcome and its provenance, never the evaluator
Audit-trail capture, tamper-evidence infrastructure and electronic-signature enforcement, which belong to the electronic-records model
Physical execution of deletion, purge or anonymisation; this model records the disposition decision and its policy binding only
Dataset catalogue publication, licensing negotiation, DOI minting and distribution management for collections of observations
Downstream analytics, model assimilation, forecasting and statistical inference beyond recording that a result was derived
Sensor tasking, actuation and control commands
Laboratory quality-management-system scope, accreditation status and personnel competence records
Transport-level streaming guarantees, message ordering, delivery semantics and API pagination

boundary_notes.distinction: OMS and SOSA separate the Sample (a feature used to represent another feature) from the Observation (the act). This model carries the reference from the observation to its proximate feature of interest and, where that is a sample, to the sample identifier and the ultimate feature it stands for. Sample identity, sampling act, preparation steps, sub-sampling relationships and custody remain owned by the sample model.

OMS requires an observation to name exactly one ObservableProperty, and QUDT separates QuantityKind from Unit. This model holds the reference and any observation-specific constraint or qualifier on the measurand; it does not define the property term, its dimension, its synonyms or its deprecation policy.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Unit of Measure Registry (UCUM / SI / QUDT)
boundary_notes.distinction: UCUM and QUDT are governed unit code systems. This model records which code system and code express the result, and any observation-level scaling; it never redefines units, conversion multipliers or dimensional vectors, and it must not silently convert values.

SOSA defines Procedure as a workflow, protocol, plan, algorithm or computational method, and OMS makes the ObservingProcedure a first-class feature. This model records which procedure version was executed and the execution-specific parameters; method authoring, validation and approval belong to the method model.

OMS models Observer, Host and Deployment (with deploymentReason and deploymentTime) as separate features. This model references the observer and the deployment in force at the time of the act; asset lifecycle, platform management and deployment scheduling stay outside.

VIM defines metrological traceability as a documented unbroken chain of calibrations. This model records the traceability declaration and pointers to the calibration evidence in force; it does not model the calibration act, the reference standard hierarchy or accreditation validity.

QARTOD publishes QC test procedures and flag conventions; SensorThings exposes resultQuality as a recorded property. This model stores the resulting flag, the identifier of the test and the identifier of the evaluating agent. Rule authoring, threshold configuration, execution and re-evaluation are owned by the quality-control model and never by this one.

MHRA GxP data-integrity expectations place audit trail, tamper-evidence and signature control on the records system. This model requires that a record be linkable to its audit entries and preserves the original acquisition record as an artifact, but it does not define, generate, secure or query the audit trail itself.

DCAT governs Dataset, DatasetSeries, Distribution and DataService, with licensing, access rights and versioning at dataset level. This model records membership pointers from an observation to the collection, datastream or series that contains it; catalogue-level metadata, distribution management and publication workflow stay in the catalogue model.

SensorThings binds unitOfMeasurement and observationType at Datastream level, and the OGC Timeseries Profile defines series-level defaults such as interpolationType. Series-level defaults are referenced here so a single record remains interpretable in isolation, but the series aggregate owns its own identity, extent, default resolution and completeness accounting.

This model records which retention policy applies, the disposition decision and the tombstone it leaves behind. Policy authoring, legal-hold determination and the physical execution of destruction are owned by the adopting Dimension's records policy.

functions.name: Register observation record
functions.description: Create a new observation record, resolve its identity under the model identity priority, and establish its initial lifecycle status and ownership.
inputs: Candidate master-system identifier and its issuing system
outputs: Registered observation record with a resolved primary identifier
Recorded identifier scheme and surrogate marker where applicable
preconditions: The issuing system is declared as the master system of record, or the absence of an authoritative identifier is explicitly asserted
The observation type is drawn from a named code list
An owning organisation reference resolves
effects: A durable record identity exists that later versions extend rather than replace
A surrogate identifier, where minted, is flagged so it can be superseded by an authoritative identifier later
No result content is asserted by this function alone

functions.name: Bind measurand and observation context
functions.description: Attach the mandatory referents that make the record interpretable: exactly one observable property, exactly one observing procedure, the ultimate feature of interest, and where applicable the proximate feature, sample, observer and deployment.
inputs: Observable property reference and vocabulary version
Ultimate and, where applicable, proximate feature of interest references
outputs: Bound measurand context on the record
Dimensional consistency verdict between property, quantity kind and unit
List of unresolved or ambiguous references
preconditions: The property and procedure references resolve in their owning registries
Where a sample is referenced, its ultimate feature is stated or derivable
The record is in a status that permits binding
effects: The record can be interpreted without consulting the producing system
Unresolved references are surfaced rather than silently dropped
Referenced registries are read only; their entries are not modified

functions.name: Record result value and unit binding
functions.description: Attach the result payload, its datatype and, for quantities, its unit code and code system, or record a declared absence or censoring instead of a value.
inputs: Unit code and unit code system, where the result is a quantity
Censoring bound, direction and limit reference where applicable
outputs: Result recorded with a typed payload or an explicit absence or bound
Unit binding with named code system
Validation findings where type, unit or absence are inconsistent
preconditions: The measurand context is bound
A quantity result carries a unit code and code system, or an explicit dimensionless assertion
Absence is expressed by a coded reason, never by an empty value
effects: Zero is never used to represent an absent or censored value
Any unit conversion performed is recorded with factor, offset and responsible agent
A binary or complex payload is bound by reference and digest

functions.name: Assert temporal frame
functions.description: Set and validate the several distinct times on the record, ensuring each carries an explicit offset and that event time is not conflated with capture time.
inputs: Clock and offset context at the observing location
outputs: Validated temporal frame on the record
Findings where offsets are missing, ordering is implausible or the clock context is unknown
preconditions: Every supplied time value carries an explicit offset or Z
The observing location's offset is known, or the unknown-offset convention is used deliberately
effects: Ingestion time is assigned by the receiving system and is not writable by producers
Phenomenon time, result time and ingestion time remain separately queryable
Timestamps missing an offset are rejected rather than defaulted to UTC

functions.name: Record externally produced quality outcome
functions.description: Attach a quality flag, its code list, the test that produced it, the assigning agent and the assignment instant to the record. This function records an outcome computed elsewhere and never evaluates a rule.
inputs: Flag value and flag code list identifier
Quality-control test reference and parameters in force
Assigning agent reference and assignment instant
outputs: Recorded quality flag with full attribution
Prevailing flag after precedence, with non-prevailing flags retained
preconditions: The flag value is valid within the declared code list
The producing test is identified and owned by the quality-control model
The assignment instant carries an explicit offset
effects: No rule is executed, evaluated or re-evaluated by this model
Superseded flags are retained rather than overwritten
Disagreements are surfaced to the owning quality-control process rather than resolved here

functions.name: Amend or supersede observation record
functions.description: Apply a controlled change to a released record by issuing a new version or a superseding record, preserving prior content and recording the mechanism, reason and authority.
outputs: New record version or superseding record
preconditions: The record is in a status that permits the selected change mechanism
The authorising agent holds the required role and satisfies any separation-of-duties constraint
The original acquisition record remains unaltered
effects: Prior values are never obliterated or overwritten in place
The reason and classification of every change are retrievable with the record
Notification of downstream consumers is delegated to the distribution model, not performed here

functions.name: Assess record interpretability
functions.description: Evaluate whether a record carries everything required to interpret its value in isolation, including mandatory referents, unit binding, temporal offsets, aggregation semantics and inherited container properties.
outputs: Materialisation recommendation for extraction from a container
preconditions: A target profile is named, or the model's own required-element set is used as the baseline
Container references, where present, resolve
effects: Gaps are reported as findings against the record rather than repaired silently
Inherited values are reported as inherited, never rewritten as if locally asserted

functions.name: Project record to an exchange encoding
functions.description: Produce a concrete representation of the record in a named encoding and profile, recording the encoding, the record version projected, the producing agent and any element-level loss.
inputs: Projection options such as inclusion of payloads
outputs: Encoded observation representation with a content digest
preconditions: The target encoding and profile are declared as an alignment on the record
The record passes the interpretability assessment for the target profile
effects: The encoding is treated as a projection and never becomes the source of truth
Loss, coercion or fabrication introduced by the projection is recorded rather than hidden
Projection does not alter the underlying record

functions.name: Record retention and disposition decision
functions.description: Bind the record to its governing retention policy, register any hold, and record the disposition decision and resulting tombstone. Execution of destruction is performed by the storage platform under the adopting Dimension's records policy.
inputs: Hold status and imposing authority where applicable
outputs: Recorded disposition decision with instant and authority
Tombstone specification for the destroyed record
preconditions: A retention policy reference resolves for the record, its payload and its original acquisition record
No unexpired hold blocks the decision
The authorising agent holds the disposition role
effects: This model records the decision and the tombstone; it never performs deletion, purge or anonymisation itself
References from other records to a destroyed record resolve to the tombstone rather than failing opaquely
Fields excluded from the tombstone do not survive disposition

composition.target: Observable Property / Quantity Kind Registry (candidate sibling model; not yet registered)
composition.purpose: Resolve the single observable property term and its underlying quantity kind that the observation determines. This model carries the pinned term reference, vocabulary version and the observation-specific method-dependence flag only; term definition, dimensioning, deprecation and mapping maintenance remain in the registry.

composition.target: Observing Procedure / Test Method Specification (candidate sibling model; not yet registered)
composition.purpose: Pin the procedure and version executed, plus execution-specific parameters and any recorded deviation pointer. Method authoring, validation studies, approval and withdrawal are owned by the procedure model and are not reproduced here.

composition.target: Feature of Interest entity models (site, station, material, subject; candidate siblings)
composition.purpose: Name the ultimate feature the result is about and, where indirect, the proximate feature. Feature identity, geometry history, renaming, merging and lifecycle stay with the entity model; this model records the reference and the representativeness basis.

composition.target: Unit of Measure Registry (UCUM, SI, QUDT bindings; candidate sibling model)
composition.purpose: Bind the result unit by naming both code system and code, and record any conversion applied. Unit definitions, conversion multipliers, offsets and dimensional vectors are owned by the registry; the link is required only when the result is a quantity.

composition.target: Sample / Specimen Record (candidate sibling model; not yet registered)
composition.purpose: Reference the sample observed, its position in the sub-sampling chain and the preparation state effective at the observation instant. Sample collection, preparation execution, custody and disposal lifecycles remain outside this model.

composition.target: Observer / Instrument Asset and Deployment (candidate sibling model)
composition.purpose: Reference the observer, host and deployment in force at the act, and the declared system capability with its validity context. Asset registration, maintenance, firmware and deployment scheduling are owned by the asset model.

composition.target: Calibration and Metrological Traceability Record (candidate sibling model)
composition.purpose: Record which calibration and reference materials were in force and whether the traceability chain is unbroken. Calibration issuance, validity determination, renewal and revocation belong to the calibration model; no certificate content is copied here.

composition.target: Quality-Control Procedure and Evaluation Service (candidate sibling model)
composition.purpose: Carry the flag value, the identifier of the test that produced it and the assigning agent. Rule authoring, threshold configuration, execution, re-evaluation and enforcement are owned entirely by the quality-control model; this model records outcomes only.

composition.target: Electronic Records and Audit Trail (candidate sibling model)
composition.purpose: Provide linkage from a record and its status transitions to the audit entries and signatures that independently attest to them. Audit capture, tamper-evidence, signature binding and audit query remain wholly outside this model.

composition.target: Retention and Disposition Policy of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Bind every record, payload and original acquisition record to a governing retention policy and record the resulting disposition decision and tombstone. Policy authoring, legal-hold determination and physical destruction are executed under the adopting Dimension's policy, not here.

composition.target: Observation Collection / Datastream / Time Series aggregate (candidate sibling model)
composition.purpose: Declare membership and record the effective inherited defaults such as unit, observation type and interpolation type. The aggregate owns its own identity, extent, completeness accounting and publication lifecycle.

composition.target: Dataset Catalogue publication model aligned to W3C DCAT 3
composition.purpose: Align record-level access rights, licence and versioning vocabulary with catalogue-level DCAT terms so that observations aggregate cleanly into published datasets. Catalogue entries, distributions, data services and publication workflow are not modelled here.

composition.target: OGC Abstract Specification Topic 20 / ISO 19156:2023 Observations, Measurements and Samples
composition.purpose: Declare structural alignment to the OMS conceptual schema for Observation, ObservableProperty, Observer, ObservingProcedure, Deployment and Sample. Alignment is asserted, not certified; conformance requires testing against the published requirements classes.

composition.target: W3C/OGC SOSA/SSN Semantic Sensor Network Ontology
composition.purpose: Declare vocabulary alignment for Observation, Result, FeatureOfInterest, Procedure, Sample and the system-capability and operating-conditions terms, enabling graph projection without adopting SSN's actuation surface.

Align the generation, usage, derivation and attribution statements on the record with the PROV starting-point and qualified terms so provenance is portable. Provenance stores, inference and validation services remain external.

Align status, absence reason, interpretation, reference range, component and member semantics with a widely deployed independent observation model, and record where the mappings are lossy. Clinical workflow, encounter and ordering semantics are excluded.

composition.target: Domain observation profiles (clinical, environmental, geotechnical, materials-testing; candidate descendants)
composition.purpose: Domain profiles specialise this model by constraining code lists, adding domain-mandatory parameters and tightening cardinalities. They must not restate generic identity, versioning, temporal, provenance or retention machinery, which this model already owns.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must nominate a single master system of record for observation identifiers and declare it before any record is registered; where several producing systems exist, the mapping from producing system to master identifier must be published, not inferred.

The Dimension must bind, per observation programme, the governing retention policy, the applicable data-integrity regime and the accepted unit code system and version, since none of these can be defaulted safely across regions or sectors.

The Dimension must declare which external registries are authoritative for observable properties, procedures, features of interest, units and quality-control tests, and must record the version pinned at the time of each observation rather than resolving against a moving target.

The Dimension must define the lifecycle status code list and its permitted transitions, including whether provisional real-time values are retained alongside reviewed values, before enabling amendment or supersession.

The Dimension must state whether it operates under an accreditation or regulatory regime that imposes uncertainty reporting, decision-rule disclosure or audit-trail duties, and must name the responsible authority.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use one namespace per adopting Dimension for locally minted surrogate identifiers, kept clearly separate from the namespaces of the master systems and external registries the model references. Never mint a local identifier inside a namespace governed by another authority, and never rewrite an external identifier to fit a local pattern. Where a governed IRI exists for a referenced concept, carry it verbatim alongside any local key. Namespace segments must be stable and free of dates, environment names or version numbers, so that a record exported from one deployment resolves identically in another.
registry_links: Unit code registries: UCUM code system with its version, and QUDT unit and quantity-kind vocabularies where dimensional reasoning is required.
Observable property and quantity-kind vocabularies nominated by the Dimension, with the version pinned per observation.
Observing procedure and test-method registers, including the version executed and the verification scope in force.
Quality-control test registers and their flag code lists, such as programme-specific test suites and their published flag conventions.
Coordinate reference system and vertical datum registers for any geometry carried on the record.
Organisation, agent and contact directories used for ownership, attribution and responsible-contact references.

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form of a record is the format-neutral element set defined by this model; any JSON, XML, RDF, tabular or document projection is derived and must not be treated as authoritative.
All timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds present and an explicit offset; a value whose offset is genuinely unknown uses the -00:00 convention rather than being coerced to Z.
Numeric result values are stored at the resolution actually determined; display rounding is applied at projection time and never written back into the stored value.

Unit codes are canonicalised as the pair (code system identifier and version, code string) using the case-sensitive form where the code system distinguishes case; a bare unit string without its code system is not canonical.
References are canonicalised to the identifier plus the scheme that governs it; a dereferenceable URL may be carried in addition but never replaces the identifier.
Ordered collections such as result components and payload parts are canonicalised with an explicit zero-based index; ordering must not depend on serialisation order.
patch_rules: A released record is patched by creating a new version, never by mutating the released version in place; the prior version remains retrievable.
Every patch names the changed elements, the change reason, the change classification and the authorising agent; a patch without a reason is rejected.
A patch may not alter the original acquisition record, the ingestion time or the identity of the observation act.
Changing the observable property, the observing procedure or the ultimate feature of interest is not a patch: it produces a new observation record, because the measurand is no longer the same.
Adding a later quality flag or a later interpretation is an additive patch that must not remove or overwrite the earlier flag or interpretation.
Replacing a surrogate identifier with a newly available authoritative identifier is an additive patch that retains the surrogate as an alternate identifier.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional element, an alternate identifier scheme or a new alignment declaration is backward compatible.
Tightening a cardinality, narrowing a code list or making an optional element required is breaking and requires a new model version and a migration statement.
Changing the meaning of an existing element, including redefining a status code or a flag value, is breaking even when the element name is unchanged.
A domain profile may constrain but may not relax this model's required elements, and may not redefine phenomenon time, result time or ingestion time.
Alignment to an external standard may be added or revised without breaking this model, provided existing mapping-loss notes are retained rather than silently corrected.
Deprecated elements are retained for at least one full model version with an explicit deprecation marker and a stated replacement.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the declared system of record for the observation, such as a laboratory information management system result key, an observing service observation key or a clinical result identifier; this identifier takes precedence whenever it exists and must be carried verbatim.

Governed global identifier or IRI issued by a normative registry or namespace, such as a resolvable observation IRI under a governed namespace or a persistent identifier assigned by a recognised data authority, used when no master-system identifier exists.

UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only when neither of the above exists, recorded with an explicit surrogate marker and its minting namespace so it can be superseded additively once an authoritative identifier appears.

A phenomenon time, result time, sample number, file name, run sequence or any date value is never an identifier; such values may only participate as qualifying components of an explicitly scoped composite key alongside a real identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds always present and an explicit offset or Z; a value whose offset is genuinely unknown uses -00:00 rather than being defaulted to UTC, and fractional seconds are recorded only where the producing system genuinely resolves them. Event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately and never conflated: phenomenon time is the event time in the observed world, result time is when the result became available, valid time is the interval over which the result is asserted usable, and ingestion time is assigned by the receiving system on capture, is not writable by producers, and is retained even when it differs from result time by an arbitrary latency.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Where an artifact belongs to an ordered series — payload parts of a split result, or acquisition records within a run, batch or injection sequence — the series position is recorded as an explicit zero-based integer index within the scope of the parent observation identifier, together with the acquiring or storing system that assigned any native sequence key. The native key is preserved verbatim; the index is a local ordering aid and never replaces it. Series position must not be encoded in file names, and gaps in a sequence are recorded explicitly rather than being renumbered.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries a content digest with the named algorithm, its byte size and its media form, recorded at the moment it is bound to the observation record. The original acquisition record is immutable once bound: corrections create a new record version that references it, never a rewrite. Encoded representations carry the record version and digest they were projected from, so a received representation can be matched to the exact record state that produced it, and a digest mismatch invalidates the representation rather than the record. Verification of digests is performed by the storing platform; this model records the digest and the verification outcome but does not implement the store.

policies: Semantics are storage-neutral and interface-neutral. JSON, XML, RDF, Markdown, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections of the canonical element set; no projection may introduce, remove or rename semantics, and any loss introduced by a projection must be recorded as a mapping-loss note.

A value is never published without the context needed to interpret it: measurand, unit or explicit dimensionless assertion, temporal frame with offsets, and either a quality statement or an explicit declaration that none was made. Absence and censoring are always expressed by coded reasons, never by nulls, blanks or zeros.

External standards are treated as alignments, not as conformance claims. Conformance may be asserted only where testing evidence is referenced; otherwise the alignment is marked as asserted and its known conflicts are recorded.

This model records outcomes it does not compute. Quality evaluation, decision-rule execution, audit-trail capture, notification and physical deletion are performed by the models and platforms that own them; recording a reference to any of these never confers ownership of their behaviour.
Corrections are additive. Prior values, prior flags and prior interpretations are retained and retrievable; obliteration of a released value is prohibited regardless of the storage technology in use.

read: Reading a record returns its effective values including those inherited from a container, with inherited values explicitly marked as inherited.
A read must expose lifecycle status, quality flags and any absence or censoring alongside the value; returning a bare value without them is a defect.
Reads of restricted or embargoed records return the record's existence, identity and classification but withhold the payload according to the access decision made by the access-policy model.
Reading a superseded version is permitted and must indicate that a later version exists, with a reference to it.
Reading a disposed record returns its tombstone rather than a resolution failure.
create: A record may be created only with a resolved identity, an observation type, an owning organisation and an initial lifecycle status.
Creation must capture ingestion time as a system-assigned value that producers cannot supply or override.
Creation of a record whose measurand context cannot be bound is permitted only in a provisional status that is explicitly marked as not fit for consumption.
Where the source system supplies no authoritative identifier, a surrogate is minted with an explicit surrogate marker and the minting namespace recorded.
Bulk creation from a series or stream must preserve per-record provenance; it may not attribute all records to a single synthetic act.
update: Released records are never updated in place; an update produces a new version through the amendment or supersession function.
Additive updates — later flags, later interpretations, newly resolved authoritative identifiers, additional alignment declarations — retain all prior content.
Updates that change the observable property, procedure or ultimate feature of interest are prohibited; those produce a new observation record.
Every update records the changed elements, reason, classification, authorising agent and instant with an explicit offset.
Updates are refused while the record is under a hold that the hold's imposing authority has not lifted.
delete: Records are not deleted on request. Disposition occurs only when the retention period bound to the record expires under its governing retention policy and no hold is in force; this model records the decision and its authority, and the adopting Dimension's records policy owns and executes the destruction.

The retention binding is evaluated separately for the record, its result payload and its original acquisition record, since these may carry different periods; the payload may not be destroyed while a policy still requires the record it belongs to, unless the policy explicitly permits payload-only disposition.

On disposition a tombstone is retained carrying only the record identifier, the disposition instant with an explicit offset, the retention policy reference and the authorising agent; the result value, payload, subject references and personal data do not survive.
References from other observation records or collections to a disposed record resolve to the tombstone, so that derivation chains remain honest rather than failing opaquely.

Where deletion is demanded on a legal ground outside retention — for example an erasure right or a security incident — the determination and its execution are owned by the adopting Dimension's data-protection and records policy and by the storage platform; this model records only the resulting disposition decision and tombstone and never performs, verifies or attests the destruction itself.
A hold suspends disposition entirely; disposition attempted against an unexpired hold is refused and the refusal is recorded.

roles.name: Observation Record Steward
responsibilities: Own the completeness and correctness of records within a programme, including identity resolution and binding of mandatory referents.
Approve amendments and supersessions and ensure change reasons are recorded.
Resolve duplicate and cross-system correlation questions without silently merging content.

roles.name: Metrology Authority
responsibilities: Approve the uncertainty statements, coverage parameters and traceability declarations carried on records.
Confirm that calibrations and reference materials in force at the act are correctly referenced and that chain breaks are disclosed.
Rule on whether a decision rule and its risk basis may be applied to a class of results.

roles.name: Data Quality Officer
responsibilities: Define which quality-control test suites apply to a programme and ensure their flag code lists are declared with versions.
Maintain the flag precedence rule and adjudicate disagreements escalated from records.
Verify that flags recorded on records carry test, agent and instant attribution.

roles.name: Dimension Registrar
responsibilities: Declare the master system of record, the surrogate namespace and the pinned versions of external registries.
Maintain the lifecycle status code list and its permitted transitions.
Approve model version changes and publish migration statements for breaking changes.

roles.name: Access and Retention Custodian
responsibilities: Bind records to sensitivity classifications, licences and retention policies.
Register and lift holds, and authorise disposition decisions.
Ensure tombstone content is correct and that disposed records no longer expose withheld fields.

access.default_rule: Access is denied unless explicitly granted. The default grant for an authenticated consumer is read access to record identity, classification, lifecycle status and alignment declarations; access to the result value, its payload, its subject references and its original acquisition record requires a grant that names the programme and the sensitivity classification. Write access is never a default and is granted per role and per lifecycle transition. All access decisions are made and enforced by the adopting Dimension's access-policy and enforcement models; this model declares the classification and the required grant, and does not evaluate or enforce entitlements.
exceptions: Records marked as relating to an identifiable person require an additional grant tied to the applicable data-protection regime, and the lawful-basis determination is owned outside this model.

Embargoed records expose identity, classification and expected release instant only, until the embargo expires or the releasing authority lifts it; derived products inherit the embargo unless the releasing authority states otherwise.
Records under legal hold are readable by the hold's imposing authority regardless of embargo, and are not disposable.
Original acquisition records may carry a stricter grant than the derived result, because they can contain operator identities, instrument diagnostics or unredacted context.

Where a result underpins a published statement of conformity, the decision rule reference and the uncertainty statement must be released with the result even if other elements remain restricted, since a conformity statement is uninterpretable without them.

Emergency or safety-critical access may bypass the standard grant only where the adopting Dimension has published a break-glass procedure; the bypass is recorded as an access event by the enforcement model.
audit_requirements: Every grant, denial and break-glass access must be recorded by the enforcement and audit models with the requesting agent, the scope requested, the decision and the instant with an explicit offset; this model requires that such records exist and be linkable, and does not generate or hold them.
Every lifecycle transition, amendment, supersession, disposition decision and hold action must be linkable from the record to the corresponding audit entry.
Projection of a record into an exchange encoding must be traceable to the record version and the producing agent, so that a released representation can be attributed.
Disposition must leave evidence that the retention policy and authority relied upon were the ones in force at the time of the decision.

required_fields: Master system of record and identifier scheme
Pinned external registry versions (property, procedure, unit, quality-control test)
Lifecycle status code list and permitted transitions
Retention policy binding and disposition authority
Declared alignments with tested-or-asserted markers and known conflicts
read_order: Read AGENTS.md first to learn the model name, type, and the specification, storage type, interface and processes URLs before touching any record.
Read the specification at the Specification URL to obtain the canonical, format-neutral element set and the required elements for the target profile.
Read the storage description at the Storage type URL to learn how the canonical elements are projected into the deployed store, and treat that projection as non-authoritative for semantics.
Read the interface description at the Interface URL to learn the available read and write operations, their scopes and their access requirements.
Read the processes description at the Processes URL to learn the permitted lifecycle transitions, amendment mechanisms, disposition procedure and escalation routes before performing any write.
Resolve the pinned external registry versions and the master system of record before binding or interpreting any measurand context.

coverage.claim: Covers one observation act and the measurement record documenting it, as enumerated by a single provider: 6 bundles, 13 layers, 29 findings, 115 questions, 3 artifacts and 9 functions spanning identity, measurand binding, result and unit, uncertainty and metrological traceability, temporal frame, geometry and operating conditions, quality flags, lifecycle, provenance, ownership, access, retention and standard alignment. Coverage is claimed only for what is actually enumerated. Alignment is asserted and not tested, the published OMS/ISO 19156:2023 text was not read, and one whole layer (uncertainty, traceability and conformity) is unreachable through the declared function set. This is not a completeness claim over the observation domain.

checklist.notes: Identity priority names the authoritative master-system identifier first, then a governed global identifier or IRI, then a Dimension-minted UUID or ULID with an explicit surrogate marker. Record identity is separated from the identity of the observation act, and dates, run numbers and file names are explicitly excluded as identifiers. Cross-system correlation and duplicate reconciliation are modelled without silent merging.

Status codes, permitted transitions, transition authority and separation of duties are modelled, along with the distinction between provisional real-time and reviewed delayed-mode records. Amendment, supersession and retraction are additive and preserve prior content. FHIR status codes are used as an alignment and counterexample rather than adopted normatively.

Relationships to feature of interest (proximate and ultimate), sample and sampling chain, procedure, observer, host, deployment, source observations, composite parents and members, and containing collections or datastreams are all modelled as typed references with an explicit statement of which model owns each target.

Phenomenon time, result time, valid time and system-assigned ingestion time are separately modelled, each requiring RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset, with the unknown-offset convention stated. Aggregation duration, interpolation type, cumulative flags and sampling regime cover resampling semantics, and clock context covers offset and drift.

Generation, usage and derivation are aligned to PROV-O; processing version and reprocessing history are modelled; the original acquisition record is retained as an immutable artifact bound by digest so a reported value can be traced to what was actually produced.

Owning organisation, attributed agents with delegation, per-part authoritative source mapping and responsible contact are modelled as references to directory models. The WIGOS practice of different organisations being authoritative for different metadata categories is reflected in the authority mapping.

Dimensional consistency between property, quantity kind and unit; declared-type versus payload conformance; acceptance criteria and supporting controls, blanks, spikes and replicates; method verification scope; and an interpretability assessment for standalone extraction. Validation findings are reported, never silently repaired.

Sensitivity classification at record and payload level, access rights and licence, personal-data indicator, embargo with release authority, and a deny-by-default rule scoped to bundle, layer, finding and artifact. Enforcement and entitlement evaluation are explicitly delegated to the access-policy and enforcement models.

Retention policy binding is mandatory and evaluated separately for record, payload and original acquisition record. Holds suspend disposition. Disposition records decision, instant and authority and leaves a tombstone carrying only identifier, instant, policy reference and authority. Execution of destruction and any erasure-right determination are owned by the adopting Dimension's records and data-protection policy and the storage platform.

Alignments to OMS/ISO 19156, SOSA/SSN, SensorThings, the OGC Timeseries Profile, FHIR R5, PROV-O and DCAT 3 are declared with tested-or-asserted markers, element-level mapping-loss notes and recorded conflicts. Encoding is treated strictly as a projection with a digest binding it to the record version it came from.

Result geometry is distinguished from observer position; coordinate reference system, vertical datum, coordinate epoch and axis-order convention are required alongside any geometry; positional uncertainty and inherited-position risk are modelled. Site and station geometry management remains in the entity models.

Uncertainty kind, value, coverage factor, coverage probability, distribution or effective degrees of freedom, and the evaluating budget reference are modelled, as is a declared omission with its ground. Traceability records the stated reference, the calibration in force, reference materials and any chain break, all by reference to the calibration model.

Unit binding requires both code system with version and code, with the case-sensitivity form where relevant; quantity kind is separated from unit for dimensional checking; series-versus-record unit conflicts have a precedence rule; conversions must be recorded with factor, offset, rounding and agent.

checklist.dimension: result absence, censoring and non-numeric results
checklist.notes: Coded absence reasons, censoring with direction, bound and limit kind, detection and quantitation limit references, suppression markers, and an explicit prohibition on encoding absence as zero or an unexplained null. Nominal properties without magnitude are distinguished from quantities.

Flags carry value, code list and version, level, producing test, assigning agent, instant and precedence outcome, with disagreements retained. Original-record immutability, contemporaneous capture and controlled amendment reflect data-integrity expectations. Evaluation, enforcement and audit-trail capture are explicitly excluded.

Confidentiality classification, embargo and grant requirements are modelled, but cryptographic signature semantics, key management, non-repudiation and integrity attestation beyond a recorded content digest are deliberately left to the electronic-records and platform-security models. No signature scheme is specified here and none should be inferred.

known_omissions: The published normative text of OGC 20-082r4 / ISO 19156:2023 was not read directly: the OGC HTML exceeded the fetch size limit and the ISO catalogue page returned HTTP 403. Class names and property multiplicities are grounded in OGC working feature-catalogue material explicitly marked draft and dated 2021-08-20, and every cardinality claim in this model must be re-verified against the published requirements classes before the model leaves candidate status.

WMO-No. 1192, the WIGOS Metadata Standard, was verified only through a WMO Information Management team wiki page and not through the publication itself; the ten metadata categories are therefore treated as indicative and not cited as normative structure.

The JCGM 200 (VIM) and JCGM 100 (GUM) full texts could not be parsed from their PDFs; metrology terms are grounded in the BIPM JCGM publications index and in ILAC guidance that restates the requirements, so individual clause numbers are not cited.
The QARTOD flag manual PDF could not be parsed; flag semantics are grounded in the IOOS project page and treated as a community convention, not an international standard.

Domain-specific observation profiles are not modelled: clinical coding systems, INSPIRE profiles, geoscience and geotechnical observation profiles, and remote-sensing product conventions are all left to EXTEND descendants.
Sensor tasking and actuation, present in SOSA and in SensorThings Part 2, are excluded entirely; a model that must both observe and command will need a sibling actuation model.
Uncertainty propagation methods, including Monte Carlo propagation and multivariate output quantities, are referenced but not modelled; only the resulting statement is carried.
Streaming delivery guarantees, event ordering at transport level, back-pressure and API pagination are excluded as interface concerns.
Cost, effort and instrument-time accounting for an observation are not modelled.
Multi-language labelling and localisation of codes and statements are not addressed.
conflicts: OMS and SOSA expose resultQuality and metadata as open, untyped slots, whereas ILAC guidance and accreditation practice require specific uncertainty content and an identified decision rule. This model carries both and claims conformance to neither.

SensorThings binds unitOfMeasurement and observationType at Datastream level while OMS and SOSA permit per-observation results; round-tripping between them can either lose per-observation unit information or fabricate it. This is recorded as a mapping-loss case rather than resolved.

FHIR R5 Observation.effective[x] and issued do not map one-to-one onto phenomenon time, result time and valid time; issued behaves closer to a publication or ingestion time, so a naive mapping silently changes temporal meaning.

UCUM and QUDT are independent unit systems with overlapping but non-identical identifiers and different treatment of annotations and arbitrary units; a record may need both bindings, and they can disagree.

QARTOD primary flags, WMO data-quality categories and FHIR interpretation codes are mutually incompatible code lists addressing overlapping concerns; no single flag vocabulary is adopted, and the code list must always be named with its version.

The OGC working feature catalogue shows most Observation properties as 0..* with constraints requiring exactly one of several key properties, which conflicts with the tighter mandatory cardinalities implied by SensorThings and FHIR. Until the published standard is read, this model states required elements on its own authority and marks the discrepancy.
PROV-O uses xsd:dateTime, which permits a timestamp without an offset, whereas this model requires an explicit offset under RFC 3339; projections to PROV must not drop the offset.
regional_assumptions: MHRA GxP data-integrity expectations are UK-specific and, for GLP facilities, the OECD advisory document takes precedence; equivalent obligations elsewhere differ in detail and the adopting Dimension must bind the applicable regime rather than assuming this one.

ILAC guidance applies where the laboratory operates under an accreditation body signatory to the ILAC arrangement; observations produced outside accreditation carry no such obligation and their conformity statements have different standing.

WIGOS metadata expectations apply to WMO member observing programmes; they are used here only as evidence that observational metadata is categorised and multi-authority, not as a universal requirement.
QARTOD conventions originate in US ocean observing and are not international standards; other regions use different flag schemes.

Personal-data implications of observations about identifiable people depend entirely on the applicable data-protection regime, which is not assumed; the lawful-basis determination is placed outside this model.
UCUM is dominant in health informatics while SI symbols and QUDT dominate in engineering and physical sciences; the default unit code system must be declared per Dimension rather than assumed.
Coordinate reference frames may be dynamic in some jurisdictions, which is why a coordinate epoch is modelled; deployments in static-frame regions may leave it unset.
adversarial_checks: Tested whether a unit should be mandatory on every observation. OMS, SOSA and FHIR all admit categorical, boolean and complex results, and VIM distinguishes nominal properties from quantities, so a mandatory unit would be unsupported. Unit binding is therefore conditional on the property being a quantity, with an explicit dimensionless assertion required rather than a silent omission.

Tested whether recording resultQuality implies ownership of quality evaluation. SensorThings exposes resultQuality as a recorded property and QARTOD publishes test procedures as a separate programme, so the evaluator is demonstrably a different thing from the record. Rule authoring, execution and re-evaluation were moved out of scope and into a REFERENCE link, and the quality function was renamed to record an externally produced outcome.

Tested whether FHIR Observation.status could serve as a universal lifecycle code list. It is healthcare-scoped and not normative outside FHIR, so the lifecycle is modelled abstractly with the Dimension declaring its own code list, and FHIR is retained only as an alignment with a recorded mapping risk.

Tested whether phenomenon time and result time could be collapsed into a single timestamp. OMS, SOSA and SensorThings all keep them distinct, and the Timeseries Profile shows aggregation intervals differing from result instants, so collapsing was rejected and a fourth time — system-assigned ingestion time — was added because MHRA-style contemporaneity requires capture time to be independently attested.

Tested whether an uncertainty budget should be an artifact of the observation record. Budgets are established per method and per matrix, not per result, so holding one here would create a second copy that could diverge from the validated one. The budget was left as a reference to the method model and only the resulting statement is carried.

Tested whether the model should own deletion. It cannot: retention policy authoring, legal-hold determination and physical destruction all sit with the adopting Dimension and the storage platform. The delete rule was rewritten to record a disposition decision and tombstone and to name the external owner of execution.

Tested whether declaring an encoded representation as an artifact violates format-neutrality. It does not, provided the encoding is explicitly a projection carrying the record version and digest it was made from and never the source of truth; that constraint was written into the artifact description, the canonicalisation rules and the projection function.

Searched for a counterexample to the proximate-versus-ultimate feature distinction being necessary. Direct in-situ observation makes them identical, but OMS retains both because indirect observation through a sample is the general case; the proximate reference is therefore optional rather than removed, with a representativeness basis required when the two differ.

providerPolicy.scope: Queued subject-model research from WM-XCT-013 onward

waived_providers.reason: The repository owner explicitly instructed the research queue to continue without Grok after repeated structured-output failures.

providerPolicy.review_rule: Claude-only results require a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remain reviewable drafts with a visible single-provider hold.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Two independent axes must not be collapsed. Record plane: the frozen registry value standalone-mm says only that this is a self-standing meta-model record rather than a fragment, mixin or profile of another entry; it classifies the registry row, carries no subject semantics and is not in the schema enum, so it cannot be reused as the subject kind. Subject-model plane: the defensible schema kind is event. OMS/ISO 19156 and SOSA/SSN define an Observation as the execution of an observing procedure, and this result's own rules are act-anchored: a patch may not alter the identity of the observation act, and changing the observable property, procedure or ultimate feature of interest is explicitly not a patch but a new observation because the measurand has changed. That is event identity. The entity reading was tested and rejected: versioning, status transitions, amendment, supersession, retention and access look entity-like, but they govern the documentation of an immutable occurrence, which is exactly what a governed event record needs under a data-integrity regime, and the result already forbids in-place mutation of released content. Aggregate was rejected because the series, datastream and collection are explicitly disclaimed and own their own extent and completeness accounting; relationship was rejected because the record carries result, uncertainty, provenance and lifecycle of its own rather than only binding referents; registry, classifier, mixin and pattern do not fit a single concrete occurrence record. The published draft must state both axes so descendants do not treat the record plane label as a subject kind.

decisions.concept: Subject-model entry kind: event, against the frozen registry value standalone-mm
decisions.rationale: standalone-mm classifies the registry record plane and is not a schema kind. The subject is the observation act; identity is anchored on the immutable measurand triple of property, procedure and ultimate feature of interest, and the result's own patch rules treat any change to that triple as a new observation rather than a version.

decisions.concept: Splitting into a separate Observation Act (event) and Measurement Record (entity) model
decisions.rationale: OMS, SOSA, SensorThings and FHIR all address the act and its record as one thing. A split would create a mandatory one-to-one pair, duplicate identity resolution across both halves, and break the existing rule that a measurand change yields a new record rather than a new version of a shared act.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root scoped to the single observation record, with series, datastream and collection excluded
decisions.rationale: Membership is carried as outbound references plus effective inherited values, and the container keeps its own identity, extent and completeness accounting. The SensorThings datastream-level unit and observation-type binding is handled as a recorded mapping-loss case rather than absorbed, which keeps the boundary honest.

decisions.concept: original-acquisition-record claimed as an artifact of one observation record
decisions.disposition: flagged defect, accepted only with a stated cardinality
decisions.rationale: The identity strategy names run, batch and injection sequence keys, which routinely span many observations, so the artifact is many-to-one against the record that claims it. The draft must state the sharing cardinality and that immutability enforcement belongs to the electronic-records model, which the same result places out of scope.

decisions.disposition: flagged defect, correction required before candidate exit
decisions.rationale: Parent observation identifier plus encoding and profile identifier plus projected record version does not distinguish two projections of the same version made at different instants by different agents. The projection function already records agent and loss, so agent and instant, or the content digest, must be part of identity rather than adjacent metadata.

The artifact identity strategy leads with the payload locator issued by the storing system, while the model's own identity priority states that a file name, run sequence or similar value is never an identifier. Digest plus parent observation identifier plus zero-based part index should lead, with the locator retained as a resolution aid only.

decisions.concept: Uncertainty, traceability and conformity layer has no function
decisions.rationale: Three findings and twelve questions covering the model's distinctive metrology value are unreachable through the nine declared functions, and hold, embargo and derivation binding are similarly thin. No function may be added in single-provider mode, so this is carried as deferred research and a visible draft note rather than repaired here.

decisions.concept: access.scopes of bundle, layer, finding and artifact against an element-level default grant
decisions.rationale: The declared scopes are context-structure planes of the model document, while the default rule grants over instance elements such as identity, classification, status, result value, payload, subject references and the acquisition record. Without a stated mapping the deny-by-default rule is not enforceable by the access-policy model it delegates to.

decisions.concept: Unconditional release of decision rule and uncertainty alongside a published conformity statement
decisions.rationale: The exception is grounded in ILAC guidance, which the same result's regional assumptions limit to laboratories under an ILAC-arrangement accreditation body. Stated unconditionally in access.exceptions it over-claims, so it must be conditioned on the adopting Dimension's declared accreditation or regulatory regime.

decisions.concept: Cardinality grounded in the draft 2021 OGC working feature catalogue rather than published OMS/ISO 19156:2023
decisions.rationale: The anchor source of the entire boundary argument was not read: the OGC HTML exceeded the fetch limit and the ISO catalogue returned 403. The result discloses this and states required elements on its own authority, which is defensible for a draft but must not survive into candidate exit unverified.

decisions.concept: Composite source identifiers SRC-008 (seven JCGM documents) and SRC-012 (two ILAC guides)
decisions.rationale: One source id standing for several distinct publications makes every source_refs entry non-specific and makes the admitted absence of clause-level citation impossible to repair. Splitting into per-document ids is a prerequisite for any later conformance evidence.

decisions.concept: Registry placement under NAV.PHY.MAT.OBS with a WM-MAT identifier prefix
decisions.rationale: The evidence base spans geospatial, clinical, oceanographic and meteorological practice and the model is used as a cross-cutting substrate, which the materials nav path and MAT prefix understate. The registry record is frozen, so this is raised for the registrar rather than changed here.

decisions.concept: Empty frozen relationship contract against eleven asserted neighbour boundaries
decisions.rationale: The result names eleven owning neighbours and describes REFERENCE links to them, while parent_ids, contains_ids, aligned_model_ids and relations_ref are all empty and the contract is an empty array. The ownership boundary is therefore prose-only and unenforced, which the draft must state plainly.

decisions.concept: Tombstone treated as evidence of disposition while destruction is disclaimed
decisions.rationale: The audit requirement that disposition leave evidence of the policy and authority in force sits close to the disclaimer that this model never verifies or attests destruction. The draft must say the tombstone records a decision, not an erasure attestation, and that a persisted identifier may itself require assessment under the applicable data-protection regime.

decisions.concept: Absence and censoring expressed by coded reasons, never by null, blank or zero, and unit binding conditional rather than mandatory
decisions.rationale: Both survived challenge on their own evidence: nominal properties without magnitude and categorical or complex results make a mandatory unit unsupportable, while a censored or absent value silently encoded as zero is the specific failure this rule exists to prevent. The explicit dimensionless assertion closes the silent-omission path.

publicationHolds: Single-provider hold: Grok was waived by the repository owner on 2026-08-29 after repeated structured-output failures, so no independent second-provider review exists. The registry provenance line also credits a prior Claude adversarial audit, and this audit is likewise Claude, so every adversarial pass on this model is same-provider. The draft must carry this on its face and must not be read as cross-provider corroborated.

Live source and version verification hold: all sixteen source URLs, retrieval dates and version pins must be re-verified before publication, with specific attention to SRC-001 OMS 3.0 / OGC 20-082r4 / ISO 19156:2023, SRC-003 SOSA/SSN 2023 Edition, the SRC-008 JCGM set including the claimed JCGM 100:2008 Amd.1:2026, SRC-009 UCUM 2.2, SRC-010 QUDT 2.1 and the SRC-002 raw GitHub draft catalogue dated 2021-08-20.

Cardinality hold: the published normative OMS/ISO 19156:2023 requirements classes were never read. Every required-element and multiplicity claim rests on a draft working catalogue marked draft and dated 2021-08-20, and the result itself records a conflict between that catalogue's 0..* properties and the tighter cardinalities implied by SensorThings and FHIR. The model may not leave candidate status until each cardinality is re-verified against the published text.

Relationship-contract hold: the frozen contract is empty while the result asserts eleven owning neighbours and describes REFERENCE links to sibling models that are not registered. The draft must state that the ownership boundary is currently narrative and unenforced, and no downstream model may rely on those links until the contract is populated.

Artifact-identity hold: the encoded-observation-representation identity strategy cannot distinguish repeated projections of the same record version by different agents, the result-payload-object identity contradicts the model's own rule that a locator or file name is never an identifier, and the original-acquisition-record is many-to-one against the observations that claim it. These three defects must be corrected or explicitly disclosed in the published draft.

Entry-kind hold: the frozen registry carries entry_kind standalone-mm, which classifies the record plane only. Publication must state the subject-model kind as event alongside the record-plane value, so that no consumer treats standalone-mm as a semantic classification of the observation itself.
Independent second-provider review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this Claude-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Obtain and read the published OGC 20-082r4 / ISO 19156:2023 requirements classes directly, then re-derive every required element and multiplicity in this model against them and retire the 2021 draft feature catalogue as the cardinality basis.

Split the composite source identifiers into one id per publication (JCGM 100, 101, 102, 106, 200, GUM-1, GUM-6; ILAC-G8 and ILAC-G17 separately), obtain parseable texts of GUM and VIM, and re-attach clause-level citations to the uncertainty, measurand and traceability findings.

Design an uncertainty, traceability and conformity function for the next revision so that the whole layer is reachable through the function set, together with functions for identifier resolution and duplicate reconciliation, provenance and derivation binding, and access classification, embargo and hold registration.

Verify WMO-No. 1192 WIGOS Metadata Standard and the QARTOD flag manual from their publications rather than a wiki page and a programme landing page, and re-assess the findings that currently lean on SRC-015 and SRC-016 as one of only three or four refs.

Refer the registry placement to the Dimension Registrar: NAV.PHY.MAT.OBS, the PHY.MAT.OBS domain tags, the WM-MAT identifier prefix and the 0.00 robotics factor all understate a model whose evidence spans geospatial, clinical, oceanographic and meteorological practice and whose SOSA grounding is sensor-centric.

Resolve whether measurement uncertainty is taken into account in the conformity decision (guard-band treatment under ILAC-G8) needs its own question, since the current interp-decision-rule and interp-risk-basis pair records the rule and the accepted risk but not how uncertainty entered the judgement.

Populate the relationship contract with the eleven asserted neighbours, assigning link types and stating which side owns each referent, so the ownership boundary becomes machine-checkable rather than prose.
